# Cornelia Bryant

## Overview

- **Age:** Over fifty years old (vol 1); fifty-nine (vol 2)  <sub>[v1 c9 P44](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0044), [v2 c26 P43](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0043)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c9 P0](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c25 P0](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c1 P57](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0057), [v2 c26 P27](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0027)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife and community organizer  <sub>[v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c14 P5](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Cornelia  <sub>[v2 c6 P27](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0027)</sub>

## Appearance

Cornelia Bryant is a fresh, round-faced woman with a pink-and-white complexion and jolly brown eyes, having fair hair worn in a hard little knob with a tight elastic hat-band. She is stout and eventually grows snow-white hair, yet retains a youthful vigor and a sharp, lively demeanor. She is noted for dressing in out-of-date or striking garments, such as chocolate print wrappers with pink roses, without caring for fashion.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P2](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0002), [v2 c6 P12](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0012), [v2 c8 P47](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0047), [v2 c26 P43](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0043), [v2 c30 P3](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0003)_

## Personality

Cornelia is sharp-tongued, outspoken, and famous for her staunch man-hating and anti-Methodist prejudices. Despite her sarcastic and blunt manner of speaking her mind, she possesses a deeply kind, compassionate heart and is always the first to help anyone in trouble or distress. She is exceptionally practical, energetic, and resolute, taking charge of community projects and standing firmly by her principles. She has a keen sense of humor and delights in banter, particularly when she can get the better of her opponents.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P54](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0054), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c6 P40](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0040), [v2 c6 P41](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0041), [v2 c6 P42](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0042), [v2 c9 P3](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0003), [v2 c14 P17](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0017), [v2 c15 P39](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0039), [v2 c18 P16](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0016)_

## History

Cornelia Bryant lived for many years as an independent, outspoken spinster in Four Winds, known for her sharp opinions on men and Methodists and her deep devotion to those in distress. She took a keen interest in Anne Shirley when Anne married Gilbert Blythe and moved to the House of Dreams, becoming one of Anne's closest friends and frequent visitors. Cornelia actively supported community efforts, such as the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and church bazaars, while constantly looking after the neglected and needy, such as Leslie Moore and Mary Vance. After thirty years of courting, she finally agreed to marry her old suitor, Marshall Elliott, upon his shaving his long beard following a Liberal political victory. They married at her home, with Marshall moving into her house. Cornelia continued her benevolent work, taking in the orphaned Mary Vance to raise her, supporting the family of the new Presbyterian minister, Mr. Meredith, and assisting Anne through her joys and sorrows, including the birth and loss of her first child.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P57](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0057), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c6 P40](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0040), [v2 c8 P25](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0025), [v2 c14 P5](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0005), [v2 c25 P28](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0028), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c11 P31](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0031), [v4 c19 P21](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0021), [v5 c2 P1](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0001), [v5 c9 P44](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0044)_

## Background by volume

- Had a younger brother whom she raised after her mother's early death and who died in his twenties
- Had a youthfulness of suitors, including Marshall Elliott and Amos Grant, but remained a spinster for decades  <sub>[v2 c6 P40](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0040)</sub>
- Was a lifelong friend of Captain Jim Boyd and Elizabeth Russell  <sub>[v2 c8 P61](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0061), [v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048)</sub>
